To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the warp in the outer disc of the galaxy is due to the misalignment between its angular momentum vector and that of the inner gas disc and that the misalignment is due to the angular momentum of the hot gas in the halo.
the warp in the outer regions of disc galaxies is a consequence of gas accretion, and that the warp feeds the inner disc and forms a low metallicity stellar component.

the outer disc of a disc galaxy is warped and misaligned with the inner disc, that the warp is a result of the misalignment of the inner disc and surrounding hot gas halo, that the outer disc feeds the inner disc via angular momentum losses, and that the warped disc forms a thick disc.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of disc galaxies in cosmological simulations, with a particular focus on the outer regions of disc galaxies and the role of misaligned components.
a detailed study of a single disc galaxy forming in the context of a high-resolution fully hydrodynamic cosmological simulation.
the nature of the disc formation process, and the role played by the surrounding gaseous halo in the formation of discs, and in particular, in the formation of misaligned outer disc components.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the outer disc is not a remnant of the primordial gas cloud that formed the galaxy, but a consequence of the ongoing accretion and interaction of the gas in the disc with the surrounding hot halo.
the warp is a consequence, not a cause, of the misalignment of angular momenta in the disc.
a misaligned outer component is a natural consequence of the accretion and disc formation process in a cosmological context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the misaligned outer disc is an important component of disc galaxies, and that it forms as a result of the interaction between the inner disc component and the hot gas halo in a galaxy.
the outer regions of disc galaxies are important for the disc formation processes and that their formation and evolution can be studied in high-resolution cosmological simulations.
the formation of the outer regions and the thick disc in galaxies is intimately linked to the formation of the inner disc.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inner disc is not the only site where star formation occurs in galaxies and that the outer disc can play a crucial role in the formation and evolution of galaxies.
the outer disc of a disc galaxy is a misaligned component, formed by the infalling gas that is strongly torquing the inner disc and feeding it with fresh gas.
the inner disc is a relatively stable structure, whereas the outer disc is more prone to being warped and misaligned due to its susceptibility to accretion and interaction with the hot halo.
